issues.what: The compiler read abbasid-caliphate/ledger/48 (900, vassal_start samanid-empire) with the roles reversed, so the Abbasid caliphate was drawn as a vassal of the Samanids from 900 to 999: Egypt and Syria 905-912 (about 2,770 cells), Abbasid cells in Khorasan (about 410), Baghdad and the stale Syrian-desert land to 999 in the Samanid tint. The Samanid page: the caliph recognised Ismail and gave him investiture over Tabaristan, Ray and Isfahan; the tie runs from the caliph to the Samanids, not the reverse.

Ifriqiya (about 580 cells) was nobody's land in 970 and 971: Cliopatria's 970-979 Fatimid shape starts the dossier's correction (without Ifriqiya, a Zirid viceroyalty from 972) two years too early. The pages date the departure of al-Mu'izz and the appointment of Buluggin to autumn 972 (5 Aug and 2 Oct).

Fatimid direct land in inland Saudi Arabia (Al Jawf, Northern Borders, Asir; 900-1,250 cells) from the Cliopatria 970 shape; the dossier cuts only the Hejaz. The Fatimid Caliphate page lists the Hejaz and Yemen at the peak only and says nothing of inland Arabia.

Western Desert of Egypt (New Valley and Matruh, about 2,000 cells) is Ikhshidid until the end of 969 and nobody's in 970-971 (the Fatimid gain names only the Nile Valley, the Ikhshidid loss names all Egypt). The conquest page says Egypt 'was not yet wholly under Fatimid control' in 969 and is silent on the oases.

Samanid keyframes of 900 and 911 draw Baluchistan (Pakistan, 1,234 cells), Sistan and Baluchestan (591) and Kerman (710) as Samanid. The Saffarid page has the Saffarids 'reduced to the provinces of Fars, Kerman and Sistan' after Balkh and expelled from Sistan only in 912; the Samanid page does not mention Kerman, Fars or Makran. The dossier's own text for the 900 keyframe says 'without Fars, Kerman and Sistan', which the snap does not honour.

Abbasid caliphate owns no cell from 970 to 999 after the fix: its Baghdad keyframe (40 km) loses the conflict with the Buyids by R2, so the caliph is invisible until 1135. Before the fix 760 stale cells hid this.

Later Jin takes the whole Later Tang heartland at the end of 936 (the unioned Cliopatria 936 shape, valid 936-946, overrides the dossier's Shanxi-only 936b keyframe) while Later Tang ends on 11 Jan 937; a jump 11 days early.

Size-rule conflicts won by the smaller state: banu-kanz/ikhshidid (2,717), ikhshidid/makuria (1,315), former-shu/tibetans (345, Tibetan keyframe over Sichuan), ganzhou/tang (323), later-liang/zhao (380), kingdom-of-germany/stem-duchy-of-bavaria (403), march-of-tuscany/kingdom-of-italy (462): the smaller state is the one that held the land.

Conflicts not checked against a page (budget went to the larger problems): pechenegs/rus (453), first-bulgarian-empire/principality-of-hungary (501, Banat), eastern-chalukyas/rashtrakuta-dynasty (756), seljuk-dynasty/samanid-empire at 985 (472; the dossier says the strip's extent is not on the page), buyid/samanid (770).

compiler: vassal_start picks the suzerain by Cliopatria area when the recorder holds more of the region ('recorded by the vassal (roles reversed)'); here that put the smaller Abbasid shape under the Samanid. I listed the 70 vassal and constituent relations drawn in this window and found no other reversed pair; a keyframe snap also releases only direct cells (release = own & plain & ~inK), so any wrongly tinted cells survive it
